notes:
A correctness release — and the keychain prompt is finally fixed for the right reason.

If your Mac slept while K8Secret was running, the next connection to your cluster asked for the password to a keychain you had never seen. That keychain is one the app creates for itself, with a random password that only ever exists in memory — so there was no answer you could have given. macOS locks it on sleep; the app now unlocks it with the password it already holds. If you have been seeing that prompt, this is the release that ends it.

Selection no longer moves on its own. Scaling a deployment started a rollout poll that kept reasserting itself as your selection, so clicking a different deployment mid-rollout pulled you back a few seconds later and overwrote the events you were reading. The poll now updates only its own row, keeps running while you look elsewhere, and names the deployment in its completion notice.

The same defect is fixed in seven more places, where a slow reply could land on whatever you had opened since: one resource's events under another's name, one pod's logs in another pod's pane, a namespace's pods after you had left it, and — the one that matters most in a secrets manager — one secret's decrypted values shown under a different secret's name. Saving was never at risk, because writes are conditional on the version they were read at; what was wrong was what you were shown.
